tasks.title: Northstar | Weekly commerce performance review
tasks.spec: BUSINESS SIMULATION: All figures below are synthetic. Currency is USD. Analyze one week of Northstar Commerce acquisition data. Paid Search: ad spend 2400, orders 160, revenue 12800, COGS 7040. Paid Social: spend 1800, orders 90, revenue 6750, COGS 3712.50. Email: spend 300, orders 120, revenue 9600, COGS 5280. Calculate per-channel and total revenue, orders, spend, COGS, average order value, revenue/ad-spend ROAS, spend/order acquisition cost, and contribution after COGS and ad spend. Show formulas and a Markdown table. Recommend a next-week allocation of the same 4500 marketing budget, explaining channel saturation and attribution limitations instead of assuming linear returns. Return an executive conclusion, the calculation table, three prioritized actions, and assumptions. Use supplied inputs only.

tasks.title: Northstar | 30-day inventory replenishment plan
tasks.spec: BUSINESS SIMULATION: Synthetic inventory data for a 30-day planning horizon. SKU TRAIL-MUG: on-hand 180 units, confirmed inbound 60, daily demand 20, supplier lead time 10 days, safety coverage 4 days, unit cost USD 12. SKU COMMUTE-BAG: on-hand 80, inbound 0, daily demand 8, lead time 14 days, safety coverage 5 days, cost USD 25. SKU DESK-STAND: on-hand 400, inbound 100, daily demand 10, lead time 7 days, safety coverage 3 days, cost USD 8. Define inventory position as on-hand plus inbound. Reorder point = daily demand * (lead time + safety days). Target inventory = daily demand * (30 + safety days). Suggested replenishment = max(0, target inventory - inventory position). Calculate position, on-hand days of cover, reorder point, target stock, replenishment quantity, and purchase cost for every SKU. State whether each SKU is below its reorder point and prioritize urgent action. Inbound timing is unknown: flag its impact and avoid assuming it arrives before a stockout. Return a Markdown decision table, total procurement amount, and a concise action plan. Do not place orders.

tasks.title: Northstar | Customer support routing and SLA design
tasks.spec: BUSINESS SIMULATION: Design an implementable support triage workflow using only these synthetic requirements. Business hours: Monday-Friday 09:00-17:00 UTC. Security or suspected fraud: P0, Security queue, acknowledge within 15 elapsed minutes, on-call escalation outside business hours. Delivered-but-missing shipment or a duplicate charge: P1, Logistics or Billing respectively, acknowledge within 2 business hours. Return/exchange requests: P2, Returns queue, acknowledge within 8 business hours. Product questions: P3, General queue, acknowledge within 16 business hours. Unknown or conflicting intents: Human Review queue, preserve highest plausible priority. Never refund, change an order, disclose personal information, or close a fraud report automatically. Classify these tickets: T1 'I see two charges for order NS-1042'; T2 'Tracking says delivered but nothing arrived'; T3 'Can I exchange a blue mug for green?'; T4 'Someone accessed my account and changed my address'; T5 'Does the stand fit a 15-inch laptop?'; T6 'I was charged twice and think my account was hacked'. Return an English Markdown routing table, priority precedence, business-hour deadline algorithm with examples for a Friday 16:30 UTC arrival, workflow pseudocode, retry/idempotency rules, and at least six acceptance cases. Label the output as a design, not a deployed integration.
